limitations: Developer feasibility fixture only; no torch device/backend integration.
No throughput or latency claim: full CPU integration tests were running concurrently.
Only bounded positive-dimension real float32 matmul. No batching, zero dimensions, mixed precision, gradients, device loss/cancellation recovery qualification or general shader API.
Pyodide uses runPythonAsync plus JSPI; production synchronous runPython entry still needs redesign.
Test server permits CORS for local fixture resources; production CSP/origin/resource policy remains unqualified.
CPU tracked incremental allocations are not RSS, WASM heap or GPU memory. MLP negative control is unchanged; memory gains are workload dependent.
Initial latency outliers are preserved; longer balanced controls did not reproduce the ~3% GroupNorm slowdown. No universal speedup claim.
The synthetic cleanup experiment used a0.67 prototype with identical graph/numerical bytes to0.68 and a different __init__ version literal; it is not relabeled as a fresh0.68 run.

GPU fixture only proves bounded float32 matmul brokering from an opaque Worker using asynchronous Pyodide/JSPI. No torch GPU dispatch, gradients, browser-wide support, cancellation/device-loss recovery, production CSP qualification or throughput claim.
No API growth in0.68; the separate first-order functional VJP prototype is not included.
Archived raw scripts retain original workspace paths and require documented dependencies/path adjustment for replay. Historical rejected experiments are included as historical data.
Main adoption, CI execution and deployment are not implied by local validation.
